newsitem.title: FINLAND: Bears loose in Helsinki as results fail to please.
newsitem.headline: Bears loose in Helsinki as results fail to please.

text.p: Shares ended well down in solid selling on Thursday as the mood turned decidedly sour amid overseas bearishness and as eight-month reports from a clutch of mid-sized companies failed to serve up many pleasant surprises.
The HEX index closed down 1.68 percent at 2,163.37 with volume an active 495 million markka, nearly one-third in Nokia.
In the last minutes of trade Nokia gapped down to test support at 200.00 markka, dipping to 199.00 but clawing back to close at 201.00, down eight markka or nearly four percent.
Brokers said the failure of sporting goods group Amer to offer any hope after its widely expected eight-month loss seemed to throw the switch, boosting markdowns for most companies.
Amer, which had risen ahead of its report on speculative buying, was knocked down 5.00 markka or nearly five percent to 101.00 as some operators sold on the fact, brokers said.
Forestries fell further amid shrinking hopes that their results, due next week, will offer reasons to be cheerful.
But Asko managed to buck the trend, posting solid gains.

The furniture and plastic pipes maker made up five percent of total bourse volume and touched its highest level in memory after it put in a 42 percent rise in January-August profit. Intraday it grazed 290.00 markka, and closed up 13.00 at 283.00.
And Merita continued to draw plenty of action after a U.S. roadshow sparked a powerful rally in the stock. Dipping 0.10 markka to 12.20, it held relatively well amid broad weakness.
Of companies reporting on Friday, Neste fell 1.50 markka to 92.00 but Huhtamaki held steady at 167.00.
